direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale continues the Knives Out style in paying homage to the whodunnit mystery genre while instilling some goofiness to make it entertaining; The direction on a microscale is good and honestly very profound at moments, such as the scene where Father Jud is on the phone, as it tackles issues with a crisis of faith while the characters explore their connection with Christianity; The storytelling is good and a little different from the previous Knives Out movies because, while it does use the mystery to help move the story forward and keep you engaged, the movie is more about what the truth reveals for these characters as they struggle with their crisis of faith in this investigation; It builds tension in a pretty light-hearted, shallow way, but that is kind of what you would get from a goofy mystery movie like this

performance.comments: Takes more of a backseat role in this movie as the Josh O'Connor is really the main character in this movie, but he still does a good job in continuing his role as Benoit Blanc and providing a good dynamic with O'Connor's character as they work together to solve this mystery despite their different perspectives on faith

The real star of the movie as he uses his subtly to really make you believe and care for this character who is struggling with his crisis of faith and his duty to the lord; the scene he has with the landscaper on the phone is incredibly powerful and profound as his action in that sequence really shows what Jud's priorities are and what his duty is in life, despite what is going on; his chemistry with Daniel Craig is good as they have a good dynamic in working together to solve this mystery despite their different perspectives on faith
Plays a very typical Glenn Close character that has a wide range as she shows why she has been Oscar nominated so many times
A very typical Josh Brolin performance that fills up the room and helps make the movie interesting and entertaining

She is fine, basically just a supporting character that is meant to movie the story and give Craig and O'Connor material to work with; I do not understand the hate she is getting for this performance, she is basically just there

cast.comments: Continues the tradition of the Knives Out movies having star-studded ensemble casts that work well together and have Good chemistry, a keep component for keeping the mystery alive in figuring out who did it

story.comments: The concept is a continuation of the Knives Out series but is less about the actual mystery and more about what the truth reveals, as this movie is an allegory for Johnson's own crisis of faith; The plot structure is typical of the other Knives Out movies; Character writing is really strong, as Father Jud's dynamic with Blanc shows both their perspectives on faith and provides somewhat of an outlet to show Johnson's own feelings on Christianity, while the supporting characters are what you expect from a Knives Out movie

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is strong and well-written; The humor is good as it helps make the movie feel goofy and entertaining; The symbolism is strong as the whole movie explores Johnson's crisis of faith, since the movie is less about finding the truth and more about what the truth reveals for each character's purpose and relationship with Christ, especially Father Jud; The foreshadowing is lacking in this one because the mystery is less laid out than in the previous movies, but it is still stronger than most movies in the mystery genre

score.comments: The score helps establish the tone

cinematography.comments: The cinematography feels well-controlled and intentional with what they focus on and how they shoot certain scenes; The use of light and perspective in the church to juxtapose Father Jud's optimistic nature with the light and Blanc's more pessimistic nature with the darkness, while cute and symbolic, was a little too overdone and annoying

editing.comments: The editing helps add tension and mystery to the movie and feels very typical of the other Knives Out movies

sound.comments: The sound helps establish the tone

production_design.comments: The production design builds sets that help show the beauty in churches and show how overarching religion can be in people's lives, whether it be in a good or bad way

review.pacing: The pacing is a little on the slower side as the movie is a tad bit long and could have used a cut of ten to fifteen minutes
review.climax: The climax is entertaining and typical of other Knives Out movies, although it feels a bit rushed and less thought-out
review.tone: The tone is very typical of other Knives Out movies as it pays homage to the whodunnit mystery genre, adding goofy comedy chops to make the movie entertaining
review.overall: Overall, the film is a good continuation of the Knives Out series that feels atypical of its predecessors as the movie is less about the mystery and more about what the truth reveals for the characters as they struggle with their crisis of faith, serving as an allegory for Rian Johnson's own connection to Christianity; while this movie is less thorough with its mystery and has a bit of a rushed climax, it is still very entertaining and is carried by Josh O'Connor's performance as the religious optimist Father Jud, as his dynamic with Daniel Craig's religiously pessimistic Benoit Blanc is really the heart of the movie
